title: Measurability of scalar rotation disagreement
statement: For every $t,\theta\in\mathbb R$, the set of $(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2$ for which exactly one of $x\le t$ and $\cos(\theta)x+\sin(\theta)y\le t$ holds is measurable.
replaced: For every real $t,\theta$, the set $\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:\neg(x\le t\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y\le t)\}$ is Borel measurable.
